newsitem.title: USA: US VIEW-Analysts says RBA could cut again.
newsitem.headline: US VIEW-Analysts says RBA could cut again.

text.p: While expressing muted surprise that the Reserve Bank cut rates so soon after the Australian dollar's latest rollercoaster ride, analysts here said the move had been expected and suggested further cuts were a possibility.

"It's kind of fascinating that they should do it at a time when the market is looking at the dollar at the slightest whiff of anything," said Richard Koss, an international economist with investment firm Maria Fiorini and Ramirez and Co.
"I suppose I'm a little surprised we didn't see a bit of wage data first, but they are trying hard to cast this in the light of a better inflation outlook."
Goldman Sachs' John Simpson said the RBA's optimism on inflation was "well justified".
Simpson said although the rate cut to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent came during an unusual period of currency volatility, it was in line with forecasts.

"We kind of expected it to move in the first quarter (of 1997), in fact our three month forecast has been that rates would fall to 5.8 per cent, so there's scope for another cut perhaps a little down the track," he said.
Other Wall street analysts said any further cuts would only come after sustained evidence that monetary conditions were holding steady.

Simpson agreed: "The most important thing they are saying is that they are going to counteract any additional strength in the exchange rate in an endeavour to keep monetary conditions roughly what they are now."
